gaps.sentence: You are ___ a big risk if you invest all your money in one company.
gaps.explanation: take a risk means to do something that might have a bad result.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.

gaps.sentence: It took him months to ___ the habit of biting his nails.
gaps.explanation: break a habit (or kick a habit) means to stop doing something you do regularly.

gaps.sentence: Make sure you are fully ___ of the terms before you sign.
gaps.explanation: fully aware of something is the fixed collocation meaning knowing completely.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: You should ___ track of your spending.
gaps.explanation: keep track of something means to stay informed about it.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.
